questions: What are the two records of the arrow on screen - the picture and the column?
What is the magnitude of (2, 3), and how do you know?
segments.say: A vector has size and direction. Watch the arrow move 2 right and 3 up: its column vector records exactly that, 2 over 3, and the length of the arrow is its magnitude. Tell your partner: what two things must two arrows share to be the same vector?

questions: Why must b start where a ends before we can read off the sum?
segments.say: Adding vectors: tail to head. Watch vector b slide until its tail meets the head of a: the sum is the one arrow from the very first tail to the very last head, and component by component the right moves add and the up moves add.
segments.watchFor: Students who add the magnitudes instead of the components. Send them back to the picture: the sum is a new arrow, and its length comes from its own components, not from adding lengths.

questions: What does cos theta do to |b| in the dot product formula?
What does a . b = 0 tell you about the angle between a and b?
segments.say: The dot product measures the shadow. Watch the perpendicular drop from the tip of b onto a: the shadow along a is the projection, and a . b = |a||b| cos theta picks out exactly that much of b. When the shadow shrinks to nothing, the vectors are perpendicular and the dot product is zero.

questions: What does each value of lambda give you on the line?
Why does a plane need two direction vectors where a line needs one?
segments.say: Lines and planes from a point and directions. One point plus one direction vector draws a whole line: r = a + lambda b, and lambda sweeps every real number to give every point. A plane needs two directions, and its normal vector stands perpendicular to the whole surface.

questions: The arrow moved to a new start point: name one thing that changed and two things that did not.
Which kind of vector really is pinned to the origin?
segments.say: Here is the trap, sprung on purpose: watch the arrow slide to a new start point and stay the same vector, because free vectors slide. Now work through the worksheet in pairs, checking each answer against the trap section of your student notes. Last, the exit ticket - on your own, no talking - and remember: if you can say why a slid arrow is unchanged, you have cracked today's lesson.
segments.watchFor: Moving a vector to a new start point changes it. Listen for students who say the redrawn arrow is a new vector. Point them at the components: same 2 right and 3 up, same magnitude, same direction - only a position vector is pinned to the origin.
